brief:
First, something you should know about your own app. Your 3 September Pull B only reached the review partway through this morning, after I had already written and pushed a packet built on the log ending 2 September. That packet was wrong the moment it landed — it prescribed a Pull B you had already done — and your phone would have ignored every number in it. I caught it and rewrote this one on the full log. Nothing bad reached you, but for two mornings your review was working from a session behind, and that is worth you knowing rather than me quietly fixing.

Today is Legs B. It is your first leg day in twenty-one days — the last one was 16 August, and Legs A before that on 20 August. Six push and pull sessions ran in between. The rotation has finally come back around to it on its own.

Here is the honest shape of tonight: this is a measuring session, not a hitting session. Every leg number in this app was set at your old gym, and your 3 September log proves the new place is on different scales — your close-grip pulldown read 127.5 in the old building and 77, 83 and 88 in the new one. Same lift, same name, completely different machine. So the weights below are starting points to find the new numbers from, not targets to chase. Log what the machine actually reads. One honest session at the new gym is worth more to me than six weeks of carried-over figures.

The RDL. Your load trainer wanted four sets and had already cut the weight hard, from 205 down to a 175 top. Your recovery trainer objected on fatigue grounds — first heavy hinge in three weeks, opening the session, with three more sets of hamstring work behind it. I took the recovery side: three sets, not four, at 135, 155 and 175 for ten. You have no smith machine at the new gym, so do the hinge the room actually allows and finish the top set with three reps still in you. On the leg press I went the other way and kept three sets, because your recovery trainer's own point was that the first set is for finding the number — and two sets total would leave you exactly one working set on your biggest quad movement after three weeks off.

You asked a question on 16 August that nobody answered: whether four sets of leg curls on the same day as RDLs was too much hamstring. You were right, and you should have had an answer then. Legs B already carries three curl sets rather than four, and tonight the RDL is cut to three as well, so the hamstring load on this day is lower than the one you queried. Legs A keeps four curl sets and has no hinge on it, which is why it stays.

Three Yes/No cards are waiting on your plan screen, all the same problem. Four of your sessions open with a lift named for a smith machine you no longer have. Your program trainer wants to swap the Legs B RDL to a barbell deadlift at three sets of eight to ten, the Push B smith overhead press to the dumbbell press you already did on 2 September, and the Pull B smith row to the wide seated cable row. Answer them on your phone and the program follows you to the new gym instead of describing the old one. The Push A smith incline press has the same problem and no fix yet — there is no incline press in the exercise list to swap it to, so that one stays broken until a new one is added.

One more thing, said plainly. On your 3 September log, ten sets carry timestamps inside a twenty-three second window, and the straight-arm pulldown's first set is stamped five seconds before the row that supposedly came first. Those sets were typed in rather than logged as you lifted them. That is fine as a record of what you did, but it means that day's rest times, its twenty-seven minutes and its exact weights cannot be trusted enough to progress from, which is part of why so much of tonight holds instead of climbing. Tapping the sets as you finish them is what turns this from a diary into something that can actually coach you.

Housekeeping: bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, fourteen days ago, at 207. With the show on 1 March that is the one trend I cannot get anywhere else. Step on the scale this week. Easy cardio twice, twenty to thirty minutes.

proposals.why: Your new gym has no smith machine, so tomorrow's leg day opens with the barbell deadlift instead — 3 sets of 8 to 10, lighter and higher-rep than your Pull A sets of 5 to 6.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells at 45 and 50 into a slot whose history says 135 on a smith machine you no longer have — this renames the slot to the dumbbell press you are actually doing, 4 sets of 8 to 10.
Pull B opens with a smith row the new gym does not have, so it becomes the wide seated cable row — 4 sets of 8 to 10, heavier and lower-rep than the same row on Pull A.

The cable lateral raise is the only side-delt work on Push A and it has drifted to seventh of eight — on 27 August the session ended after the sixth exercise, so your side delts got nothing that night while your rear delts got all three sets; this moves it up to fifth, straight after the shoulder press.

overrides.reason: Three sets tonight, not four. This is your first heavy hinge in three weeks and it opens the session with three more sets of hamstring work behind it, so your recovery trainer objected to the fourth set and I agreed. The 205 from 16 August was set on the old gym's smith machine and does not carry to a new bar, so this re-enters at a weight you can verify. Finish the top set with three reps still in you.

Three sets stay. On 16 August you went 12, 11 then 10 at 180, so the third set failed and no increase was earned. Trust the 3 sets of 10 to 12 as the instruction and treat 180 as an old-building stack position — the first set is for finding what this machine reads, not for hitting a number.

You genuinely earned a jump here — 142.5 for twelve on all four sets on 16 August, and thirteen twice on 20 August. But 150 is a pin on a machine you no longer use, so holding at 142.5 lets the first set re-establish the scale instead of guessing at it. Three sets, which is already fewer than the four you queried back in August.

The app would have asked for fifteen reps at 135, a number you have never hit — on 20 August both sets stopped at thirteen. This asks for the thirteen you have actually done. Expect the new gym's stack to read differently and log what it says.
105 for twelve and twelve on 20 August sits at the bottom of the range, so nothing was earned even on the old machine. Same two sets, and useful groin work before a first hinge back.

The app would have printed fifteen reps at 300 three times, which you have never once produced — it was twelve, twelve, twelve on 16 August and thirteen, thirteen, twelve on 20 August. This corrects the target down to what you have actually done. Three sets, not four.

On the old cable stack you had earned 65 — sixty for twelve, then thirteen on 20 August. But cables are exactly where the gym change bites hardest: your pulldown went from 127.5 to the high seventies and eighties on 3 September. Holding at 60 means the first set measures the new stack rather than guessing.

The one slot tonight that the gym change cannot touch, because bodyweight travels between buildings. Twelve and twelve on 16 August, thirteen and twelve on 20 August, so this asks for one more rep on each set. It is the only real progression on the card.

dissent.progression: Four sets at 135, 155, 175 and 175 for ten — the weight is already cut hard from 205 because the old smith machine's number does not carry to a new bar.
dissent.recovery: Cut to three sets and raise a fatigue objection: first loaded hinge in twenty-one days, opening the session, with three more sets of direct hamstring work behind it.
dissent.why: Recovery is right about the shape and progression is right about the ladder, so I took recovery's set count and used progression's weights for the three sets that survive. The objection was on fatigue grounds, which I am allowed to overrule, and I chose not to: the fourth set buys almost nothing on a night whose real job is finding out what the new gym's equipment reads, and the cost of getting this wrong is measured in weeks. He also asked in August whether this day carried too much hamstring work. It did. Cutting the hinge rather than the curl answers that question in the direction he raised it.

dissent.progression: Three sets at 180 for twelve — the third set failed at ten on 16 August, so nothing was earned and the weight repeats.
dissent.recovery: Two working sets, not three, coming back from three weeks off, with the first set used to find the new machine's number.
dissent.why: I ruled against recovery here using recovery's own argument. It said the first set at a new gym is for finding the number rather than hitting one — which means three sets yields two real working sets, exactly what it asked for. Cutting to two would leave him a single working set on his biggest quad movement after twenty-one days without one. The brake belonged on the hinge, where the injury risk actually is, and I already applied it there.
